manual_activity: Resolve and approve the source Get/GET versus ClearLog POST conflict, exact target/scope, required retained logs, maintenance window and irreversible evidence-loss acceptance before any action.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek's POST interpretation matches ClearLog action semantics but cannot override the preserved Master's Get/GET identity without recording the conflict and obtaining approval; the source paths and Log1 assumption are also untrusted.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After exact action discovery, verified pre-clear archive and explicit approval, send one schema-valid POST to the selected LogService's canonical ClearLog target and verify scope read-only; never run the source GET.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Manager/LogService ClearLog target and 15/10 timing remain, but no instance, payload, archive scope or recoverability is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Separate discovery/backup from a single approved ClearLog POST and a read-only scope audit.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the GET/POST conflict explicit, removes automatic clearing, requires complete evidence preservation and treats timeout as unknown rather than retryable.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers one selected service's ClearLog action only; it does not prove global log retention or clearing for other services.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Deleted target entries generally cannot be restored to the BMC; the external archive preserves evidence but is not a target rollback.

project_override_considerations: A project may intentionally define this as metadata inspection instead of execution; if so it must use the following ActionInfo row and leave this destructive action unexecuted. Do not blend the two scopes.
expected_evidence: Canonical action URI, method and payload schema
Approval, maintenance window and irreversible-loss acknowledgement
Complete pre-clear export manifest, hashes and readability proof

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item is named Get, the Master Procedure sends GET, but the target names LogService.ClearLog and DeepSeek proposes POST. GET inspection and destructive POST are materially different methods and outcomes, so the conflict must remain visible.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The conflict can be resolved through an explicit owner decision and exact vendor action package; required authorization and archive inputs make this REQUIRES rather than inherently BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Prevents a misleading GET case from either silently doing nothing or deleting logs without authority, and establishes evidence preservation plus one-shot ambiguity handling.
independent_technical_reasoning: ClearLog is an action, not a readable resource whose success can be judged by pretty JSON. The Master method conflict cannot be normalized silently because GET and POST have radically different blast radii. If execution is approved, the primary safety artifact is the verified pre-clear export: target-side recovery is ordinarily impossible. A timeout cannot trigger retry because the first request may already have committed; the agent must query the service state read-only and escalate. The final scope audit must prove only the selected service changed and that the external archive remains usable.
